name: Infantile-onset Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy with Severe Cognitive Regression
aliases: Early-onset mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with cognitive decline
Infantile mesial temporal epilepsy with intellectual regression

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Infantile Mesial Temporal Lobe Epilepsy Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Onset of focal seizures originating from the mesial temporal lobe before 24 months of age
Progressive severe cognitive regression following seizure onset
MRI evidence of mesial temporal lobe abnormalities including hippocampal sclerosis or signal changes
EEG showing epileptiform discharges localized to the mesial temporal lobe
Exclusion of other metabolic, infectious, or structural causes of epilepsy and cognitive decline

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of infantile-onset focal seizures localized to the mesial temporal lobe with progressive severe cognitive regression and MRI evidence of mesial temporal lobe abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology, neuroimaging, and neuropsychological assessment.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal seizures with impaired awareness originating from mesial temporal structures
searchTerms: temporal lobe seizures with impaired awareness
partial seizures from inner temporal brain
scarring of hippocampus on brain scan
hippocampal tissue damage seen on MRI

common.symptomName: Behavioral disturbances including irritability and social withdrawal
Autonomic manifestations during seizures (e.g., epigastric rising sensation, pallor)
searchTerms: seizure-related stomach rising and pale skin
seizure causing autonomic signs like pallor

common.symptomName: Developmental delay prior to seizure onset
Refractory epilepsy with poor response to antiepileptic drugs

occasional.symptomName: Sleep disturbances including insomnia and fragmented sleep
Transient autonomic symptoms such as tachycardia during seizures

rare.symptomName: Visual field deficits related to temporal lobe dysfunction
searchTerms: vision loss in parts of visual field
visual field defects from temporal lobe
partial vision loss related to brain area

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric comorbidities including anxiety or depression

searchTerms: autonomic instability with low BP episodes

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; exclusion of metabolic or infectious causes
imaging: MRI showing hippocampal sclerosis or mesial temporal lobe signal abnormalities
FDG-PET may show hypometabolism in temporal lobe
other: EEG demonstrating focal epileptiform discharges in mesial temporal regions
Neuropsychological testing confirming severe cognitive regression

distinguishingFeatures: Infantile spasms rather than focal temporal seizures
Different seizure semiology and developmental trajectory
Acute encephalopathy with refractory status epilepticus
Diffuse brain involvement rather than focal temporal lobe

redFlags: Rapidly progressive cognitive decline in infancy
Refractory focal seizures unresponsive to multiple antiepileptic drugs
MRI evidence of progressive mesial temporal lobe damage
references: Orphanet: Infantile-onset mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with severe cognitive regression, ORPHA:391316
Engel J Jr. Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy: what have we learned? Neuroscientist. 2001
Berg AT, et al. Early-onset epilepsy and cognitive outcomes: A review. Epilepsia. 2012
